svg.title: Positive and negative charges give the same conventional current
svg.desc: (a) Positive charges move to the right, in the direction of the electric field E, through a cross-sectional area A of a wire; the conventional current I is also to the right. (b) Negative charges move to the left, opposite the field, through the area A; the conventional current I is still to the right, in the direction of the field. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: Blue arrows: carrier drift; green arrows: conventional current
I = nqAv drift, using signed q and velocity. Positive carriers moving right and electrons moving left
both give current to the right. Drift is enlarged.
Illustrative motion • slowed down • cycle restarts
